test_meta.title: ST – Practice Set C: Hemostasis, Sutures & Wound Closure

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which parameter indicates the smallest diameter suture strand according to the United States Pharmacopeia (USP) standard numbering system?
questions.explanation: In USP suture sizing, each zero added designates a thinner diameter. #7-0 is much smaller in diameter than 4-0, 2-0, or #1.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 386

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which suture size is standard for microvascular anastomosis of 1 to 2 mm digital or coronary vessels?
questions.explanation: Microvascular anastomosis of tiny vessels requires microscopic monofilament suture such as 8-0, 9-0, or 10-0 polypropylene.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 387

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which natural absorbable suture is derived from the submucosal layer of sheep intestine or serosal layer of beef intestine, treated with chromium salt solution to slow enzymatic breakdown?
questions.explanation: Chromic gut is collagen treated with chromium salts to resist rapid enzymatic digestion, extending absorption time to 10-21 days compared to plain gut (7-10 days).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 388

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Why are surgical gut sutures packaged in foil packets soaked in an alcohol-water conditioning fluid?
options: To keep the natural collagen strands pliable and prevent them from drying, stiffening, and snapping
To sterilize the suture immediately before handoff
questions.explanation: Natural gut sutures dry out and become brittle if exposed to air. The packaging fluid maintains moisture and flexibility; gut should be used promptly after opening without excessive wiping.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 389

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which synthetic absorbable monofilament suture composed of poliglecaprone 25 is celebrated for smooth passage through skin during subcuticular closure, absorbing in 90 to 120 days?
questions.explanation: Monocryl (poliglecaprone 25) is an absorbable monofilament suture with low tissue reactivity and excellent knotting, popular for cosmetically sensitive subcuticular skin closures.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 390

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which non-absorbable suture has the highest tensile strength, is biologically inert, and is used for sternotomy bone closure and tendon repairs?
questions.explanation: Stainless steel suture is completely inert, possesses the highest tensile strength of any suture material, and is standard for wiring median sternotomies and heavy orthopedic fixations.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 393

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What type of needle has a round tapered body that narrows smoothly to a sharp point, used exclusively on soft tissues like bowel, peritoneum, and subcutaneous fat?
questions.explanation: Taper point needles puncture and stretch tissue fibers without slicing, making them the standard choice for visceral gastrointestinal and vascular soft tissues.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 399

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Why are cutting or reverse cutting needles used on skin instead of taper needles?
options: Skin has a dense, tough keratinized epidermal and dermal collagen layer that requires sharp cutting edges to penetrate without tearing or bending the needle
Cutting needles create smaller puncture holes in skin
questions.explanation: Skin dermis is tough and fibrous. Taper needles cannot penetrate skin without excessive force and needle bending; cutting edges slice through the dense dermal collagen smoothly.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 401

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What type of continuous suture technique runs around the lumen of a tubular organ (such as the base of the appendix or gall bladder stump) to invert the stump when cinched tight?
questions.explanation: A pursestring suture is a continuous circular inverting stitch placed around the cecal base of the appendix; cinching it tight inverts the contaminated stump into the bowel lumen.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 406

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which interrupted suture technique forms a supportive cross-stitch that distributes wound tension across broad surfaces, frequently used for heavy fascial defect closures?
questions.explanation: Figure-of-eight sutures create a cross-brace pattern that holds tension securely over wide fascial tears or anchors heavy pedicles.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 408

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What small plastic or rubber tubing sleeves are threaded over heavy retention sutures to prevent the suture from cutting into the patient's skin under tension?
questions.explanation: Retention bolsters (plastic or rubber bridges/bumpers) cushion retention sutures against the skin, distributing high closure tension and preventing necrosis.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 410

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What is the primary cellular component that synthesizes the extracellular collagen matrix and ground substance during the proliferative phase of wound healing?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are specialized connective tissue cells that migrate into the wound bed to generate collagen fibrils, fibronectin, and glycosaminoglycans.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 413

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which phase of normal physiological blood clotting involves platelets adhering to exposed subendothelial collagen and aggregating to form a primary platelet plug?
questions.explanation: Primary hemostasis encompasses vascular spasm, platelet adhesion via von Willebrand factor to exposed collagen, and aggregation to create the temporary platelet plug.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 376

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What is the final enzyme in the coagulation cascade that catalyzes the conversion of soluble fibrinogen into insoluble, cross-linked fibrin strands?
questions.explanation: Thrombin (Factor IIa) cleaves fibrinogen peptides to yield fibrin monomers, which polymerize and cross-link to solidify the definitive blood clot.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 377

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What drug is administered intravenously by the anesthesia provider to provide systemic anticoagulation during vascular bypass clamping, and which drug acts as its specific reversal antidote?
questions.explanation: Heparin prevents clot formation during arterial cross-clamping. Protamine sulfate is a strongly basic protein that binds heparin to completely neutralize its anticoagulant effect.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 21, pg 629

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which passive gravity surgical drain consists of a flat, soft latex or silicone ribbon that allows wound exudate to drain by capillary action onto a dressing sponge?
questions.explanation: A Penrose drain is an open, passive drain that relies on capillary action and gravity to convey drainage into surrounding absorbent sterile gauze pads.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 320

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which specialized T-shaped latex drain is placed inside the common bile duct during choledochotomy to stent the duct and facilitate continuous external bile drainage?
questions.explanation: A T-tube is inserted into the common bile duct with its crossbars in the duct and long stem exiting the abdominal wall, maintaining duct patency and decompressing biliary pressure.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 510

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What is an abnormal, hypertrophic scar formation extending far beyond the original surgical incision margins, characterized by excessive, disorganized collagen deposition?
questions.explanation: Keloids are benign, raised fibrous lesions caused by excessive collagen synthesis that invade normal surrounding skin beyond initial wound boundaries, common in darker skin types.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 424

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which patient factor significantly impairs normal surgical wound collagen synthesis, angiogenesis, and fibroblast proliferation?
options: Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus and chronic corticosteroid therapy
Normothermia in the postoperative recovery unit
questions.explanation: Hyperglycemia impairs leukocyte phagocytosis, while corticosteroids inhibit the inflammatory response, capillary budding, and fibroblast collagen synthesis.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 423

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What liquid skin adhesive composed of octylcyanoacrylate (Dermabond) is applied topically over approximated skin edges to seal small incisions without staples or suture removal?
questions.explanation: Dermabond (2-octyl cyanoacrylate) is a sterile topical liquid adhesive that polymerizes into a flexible waterproof bridge over clean skin edges, sloughing off in 7-10 days.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 427

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What is the primary difference between monofilament and multifilament braided sutures regarding knot security?
options: Multifilament braided sutures have higher friction between strands and hold knots more securely with fewer throws than slick monofilaments
Monofilament sutures hold knots with only 1 throw
There is no difference in knot holding
questions.explanation: Braided sutures generate high surface friction, producing secure knots that resist slippage. Slick monofilaments require 5-6 throws to prevent unraveling.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 387

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which small titanium or absorbable clips are applied across blood vessels using a pistol-grip applier to provide rapid permanent hemostasis?
questions.explanation: Ligating clips (titanium, tantalum, or polymer) are squeezed across vessel pedicles to occlude lumens quickly in laparoscopic and open vascular procedures.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 384

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What type of dressing uses sterile petrolatum-impregnated or silicone gauze (such as Xeroform) placed directly on the wound bed to allow exudate to pass through without adhering?
questions.explanation: The primary non-adherent layer (Xeroform/Adaptic) prevents dressing gauze from sticking to delicate new epithelial cells during healing and bandage removal.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 426

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which CDC wound classification applies to a total hip arthroplasty performed in a laminar-flow operating room with primary wound closure?
questions.explanation: Elective orthopedic joint replacements are Class I (Clean) because they are uninfected, elective, closed primarily, and do not enter respiratory, GI, or GU systems.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 420

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What is the purpose of placing a wet-to-dry dressing on an infected, open surgical cavity?
options: To mechanically debride necrotic debris and slough as the dried gauze is removed from the wound
To completely sterilize the wound overnight
To prevent granulation tissue from forming
questions.explanation: In wet-to-dry dressings, moist saline gauze embeds in necrotic slough as it dries; upon peel removal, it mechanically debrides the wound bed to encourage fresh granulation.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 428

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which factor provides the greatest barrier to microorganism proliferation in healing surgical wounds?
options: Active phagocytosis by tissue macrophages and adequate microvascular perfusion
Complete limb immobilization in a fiberglass cast
questions.explanation: Macrophages phagocytose bacteria and cellular debris while releasing angiogenic growth factors; robust local blood perfusion supplies oxygen and antibiotics.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 413

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What is the typical time frame for skin suture or staple removal following an uncomplicated abdominal or orthopedic incision?
questions.explanation: Skin staples and non-absorbable sutures are typically removed at 7 to 10 days postoperatively once the epithelial seal has formed, preventing suture track scarring.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 425

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which synthetic non-absorbable braided suture coated with silicone or PTFE (trade name Ethibond or Tevdek) is preferred for heart valve sewing rings and tendon repairs?
questions.explanation: Braided polyester sutures (Ethibond) provide permanent high tensile strength and smooth handling, ideal for attaching prosthetic heart valves and anchoring tendons.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 392

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What is an abnormal epithelialized tract communicating between an internal hollow organ and the external skin surface called?
questions.explanation: A fistula is an abnormal conduit connecting two visceral epithelial cavities or an internal organ to the exterior skin (e.g., enterocutaneous fistula).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 423

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: What localized collection of extravasated blood within surgical tissue layers causes pressure, pain, and secondary infection if not evacuated?
questions.explanation: A hematoma is a localized pool of clotted blood outside blood vessels that increases wound tension, compromises microvascular perfusion, and serves as a bacterial culture medium.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 12, pg 422
